cards.text: This is a song for the choirmaster, from the sons of Korah, descendants of a Levite named Korah (Numbers 16:1). The singers are a whole “we,” and they open by saying who God is to them. No warm-up, no “testing, one, two,” just straight in.

cards.question: The singers call God their refuge and strength. What kind of help do they say He is in times of trouble?

answers.text: A help that is always there
A help that comes once a year
A help that comes when trouble ends

cards.text: Then the song goes BIG: though the earth is transformed and the mountains are toppled into the depths of the seas. Friend, I used to panic when somebody slammed the junk drawer, and these singers are talking about MOUNTAINS going for a swim.

cards.question: Because God is their refuge and strength, the singers say they will not ___

cards.text: And it keeps going: though the waters roar and foam and the mountains quake in the surge.

cards.question: True or false: the singers say they won't fear because all that shaking will turn out to be small.

cards.text: Then the song takes a breath. After all that roaring sea, there's a river, and the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells.

cards.question: After waters that roar and foam, the song shows a river whose streams ___ the city of God
The song pictures mountains toppling. True or false: it says the city of God, with God within her, will be moved too.
The song says God will help the city of God. When?

cards.text: God's already helping at dawn, while I'm slapping the oven timer and begging it for five more minutes. Then the song turns to the nations: they rage, and kingdoms crumble.

cards.question: Nations rage and kingdoms crumble. When God lifts His voice, the earth ___
Right after that, the song sings a line it comes back to at the very end. What does that line say about the LORD of Hosts?

answers.text: He is still on His way

cards.text: And the line keeps going: the God of Jacob is their fortress. That's Jacob, the father of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 49:28).
Then the song calls out an invitation, like a friend waving you over to the window. Come on, you've GOT to see this.

cards.question: What does the song call out to come and see?
True or false: every work of the LORD that the song points to is quiet and gentle.

cards.text: Not even close: He brings devastation upon the earth, breaks the bow, shatters the spear and burns the shields in the fire. The only thing I ever put in a fire was a batch of cookies, and friend, that was NOT on purpose.

cards.question: With bows broken and shields burned, the LORD makes ___ cease throughout the ___

cards.text: Then God speaks, and His first words are “Be still.” The dead batteries I shared that drawer with argued for YEARS and never managed that once.

cards.question: God says “Be still.” Along with being still, what does He say to know?
God says He will be exalted. Where?

answers.text: Among the nations and over the earth

cards.text: And the song ends on that line again: “The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our fortress.”

findings.problem: The wrong answer "A help that comes once a year" is silly next to a song that calls God a refuge, so the right answer stands out and the card tests nothing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to his drawer backstory: that he panicked when somebody slammed the junk drawer. The backstory only says they held their breath when it opened. Made-up moments are allowed around his bakery, not in the drawer story.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the BSB's word for what the streams do (delight, flood or surround). The setup doesn't let the baker reason out "delight" over "surround". The meaning could be asked instead, such as whether this river is a threat or a joy to the city.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click right away. "Slapping the oven timer and begging it for five more minutes" can read as wanting the cookies to bake longer, not as sleeping in, so the contrast with God helping at dawn gets lost. "Already" also adds a timing the text doesn't give. Verse 5 says only that God will help her when morning dawns.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the next word of the line: when God lifts His voice, the earth ___ (melts, sings or floods). Nothing told so far lets the baker reason out "melts" over "floods". It is a wording guess.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only two-part answer and is longer, and both wrong answers start with "Only", which makes them easy to rule out by form alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
